newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU envoy to seek refugee access from Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy to seek refugee access from Zaire rebels.

text.p: France announced on Friday that EU states had given the go-ahead for a European Union envoy to meet Zairean rebel chief Laurent Kabila.
"The European special envoy will visit Mr Kabila to urge him to rapidly solve humanitarian problems in eastern Zaire," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told a news briefing.

He said France shared the concern of the United Nations Security Council at the violence and deprivation in Zaire and was appalled by the rebels' refusal to let the U.N. and relief groups have free access to the refugees.
"This situation is intolerable and must end," he said.

The Security Council, alarmed by reports from Zairean villagers that rebels had killed hundreds of refugees, has harshly criticised Kabila's Tutsi-dominated rebels for preventing aid from reaching the Hutu refugees and obstructing their return home to Rwanda.
"We have demanded that the authors of the attacks and those who are responsible for them be detained and punished," Rummelhardt added.
Kabila's rebels, who have vowed to oust Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, have seized about half of Zaire since October and are advancing on the capital, Kinshasa.

Rummelhardt repeated an appeal to French nationals not to leave Kinshasa for the moment. France and Belgium have stationed troops in Brazzaville, across the river Congo from Kinshasa, to help evacuate foreign nationals should it become necessary.
